post.caption: Oscars were once made of plaster. MGM art director Cedric Gibbons designed the statuette, a knight with a sword standing on a film reel. The first awards were handed out on May 16, 1929. It stands 13.5 inches tall and weighs 8.5 pounds, and today it is bronze plated in 24 karat gold. In 1939, the Academy made the name Oscar official. For three years in the 1940s, Oscars were painted plaster, and winners later swapped them for gold plated metal ones. Winners must first offer to sell an Oscar to the Academy for $1.
